title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll landed on the thermal receipt. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every card is a different layout topology, not a restyle of the current one.

options.label: Struk Thermal
options.lineage: the thermal receipt every warung, canteen and kopdar prints
options.thesis: The console is a receipt printer: every activity prints line by line down one narrow column of paper.
options.viewport: A full-height paper column dead centre on a dark laminate counter. The six tools are numbered menu lines with dotted leaders and durations, and the running activity prints beneath them, one character at a time.
options.risk: Reads as novelty stationery the moment the print is faked rather than typed, and a narrow column throws away a projector if the type is set small.

raised.raise: From the bazaar: every catalog line carries its own stamped tag of origin, so duration and gadget-free are visible before you read the description.
From the specimen: hierarchy carried by scale alone, no ornamental framing, no card wrapped around the thing being said.
From the sampler: the tools run in bands of increasing difficulty, so a first-timer's path through them is legible on the strip itself.

regions.label: tool menu, numbered lines, dotted leaders, durations
running activity prints here, line by line

options.label: Papan Tulis
options.lineage: the classroom whiteboard and its aluminium marker tray
options.thesis: The console is the board at the front of the room: one wide surface, wiped and rewritten, written marker-huge.
options.viewport: One full-bleed board. Tools lie in the tray across the top with the active marker resting on the lip, the running activity is written enormous and left-aligned with no card around it, and catalog index cards stay clipped to the right rail, always visible.
options.risk: The direction most runs in this category land on, and a plain white board left uncommitted is indistinguishable from clean minimalism.

options.label: The Segment Wall
options.lineage: alarm clocks, gas-station price totems, scoreboards, microwave panels
options.thesis: Every number this product already owns is a digit, so the whole surface is one eight-cell mask with the unlit cells designed too.
options.viewport: A fixed band of segment cells across the top carries code, clock and queue. The main display below holds enormous live digits beside a dot-matrix prose cell. Controls are a key row along the bottom.
options.case: Room code, timer, click score and countdown are already digits, so it fuses cleanly onto the four numeric surfaces; the riddle clue and the question text cannot fit an eight-cell mask.
options.risk: Prose is what a facilitator actually reads aloud, and a dot-matrix cell is the one place this product cannot speak plainly.

options.label: Patchwork
options.lineage: pieced quilts of worn garments, every block a different body and date
options.thesis: The catalog is the only surface that ever needed a grid of cards, so it becomes a pieced quilt of unequal blocks with each caption seamed to its patch.
options.viewport: A header patch spanning most of the width carries the running activity, two narrower patches beside it hold the timer and the room code, and below them the catalog is a staggered patchwork of unequal blocks joined by visible seams.
options.case: It is the only system on the table that refuses equal blocks outright, which is exactly the disease in the current catalog; it fuses cleanly and loses only on audience identification, since pieced cloth reads craft rather than classroom.
options.risk: Craft reads cosy, and a facilitator projecting to adults needs the room to take them seriously.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.lineage: a midnight lane where merchants trade shadows
options.thesis: Goods tagged with a small ticket of origin and length, traded by light.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in a lane of traded shadows is the classroom a facilitator walks into.
options.kept: Kept the hand-marked tag of origin, raised onto every catalog line.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone, no ornament so the letterforms carry it.
options.case: Fuses thinly: it holds scale contrast but has no material world, and lands on the mono-label-plus-giant-type look this category defaults to.
options.kept: Kept scale-alone hierarchy, raised as the ban on ornamental framing.

options.label: Stitched Sampler
options.lineage: a child's alphabet sampler, each band looser than the last
options.thesis: Bands stacked in increasing difficulty, signed and dated at the foot.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a band of increasing difficulty maps onto none of the six tools, only onto the order they happen to sit in.
options.kept: Kept the increasing-difficulty path, raised onto the tool order.

options.label: Character Roster
options.lineage: a goods catalog of ranked mascots with name plates and birthdays
options.thesis: A finite ranked roster, each entry with its own name plate and one-line note.
options.case: Fuses worst of any hand: a ranked roster of characters with fixed personal furniture is the precise opposite of a room of strangers nobody has assigned a role in.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every icebreaker site ships, executed at full craft instead of at half.
canonCard.viewport: Top nav, a centred hero with one primary action, a three-up feature grid of the tools, then a footer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design, which is the point of having it on the table.
